title: Anaerobic digestion sludge sequencing
description: Anaerobic granular sludge is a key biomass form for high-rate anaerobic wastewater treatment. However, its in situ formation during waste activated sludge (WAS) digestion in continuous stirred-tank reactors (CSTRs) has generally been considered unlikely, particularly under high suspended-solids (SS) conditions. Here, we report the unexpected formation of granular sludge in the methanogenesis CSTR of a full-scale 75 t d two-phase anaerobic digestion (TPAD) system treating municipal WAS without thermal hydrolysis pretreatment. We combined physicochemical characterization, microbial community analysis, metatranscriptomics, and reactor-scale hydrodynamic calculations to resolve the granulation mechanism. Distinct dark-brown granules, mainly 500-1000 um in diameter, coexisted with floc sludge in the methanogenesis reactor. The larger granular fraction retained on a 24-mesh sieve (ADeff24) showed excellent settleability (22.01 +/- 0.21 m/h) and was enriched in inorganic components, especially Al2O3, Ca, and P, indicating ballasting and mineral-bridging effects. The total extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) content in this fraction (AD_eff_24) reached 197.70 mg/g VSS, with tightly bound EPS (T-EPS) and hydrophobic proteins (PN) as the dominant structural components. Microbial analysis showed enrichment of EPS-producing bacteria, including Thauera and Zoogloea, together with pronounced dominance of the filamentous acetoclastic methanogen Methanothrix, whose relative abundance reached 76.18% in AD_eff_24. Metatranscriptomic profiles further showed enhanced expression of enzymes involved in protein and polysaccharide biosynthesis, supporting active EPS overproduction. Mechanistic calculations indicated that acetate could fully penetrate the granules. Weak macroscopic shear, biogas-induced microshear, and implicit elutriation selection then promoted the retention of dense aggregates. These results show that spontaneous anaerobic granulation in a sludge-fed CSTR can occur through coupled substrate phase separation, microbial kinetic selection, EPS-mediated self-assembly, and organic-inorganic framework formation.
